prep.title: What to bring for ice fishing
items: Nothing blocks the wind on the ice, so it feels far colder than the thermometer says. Bring a hat, scarf and gloves and dress in layers. Check the wind chill calculator before you leave.
Waterproof winter boots, spare socks and gloves and hand warmers help you last longer. The ice is slippery, so wear low-heeled shoes.
Many venues sell rods and bait on site. A folding stool or cushion makes long sessions easier.

tickets.title: Booking and tickets
items: Ticket booths at popular ice fishing festivals get busy from early morning on weekends. If advance booking for fishing spots is offered, book ahead.
Some festivals refund part of the entry fee as local gift certificates or food vouchers. Fees and refund rules change every year, so check the official site.
Most light festivals are free, but some, like the Garden of Morning Calm, charge admission. Lights usually come on around sunset.

safety.title: Ice thickness and cancellations
items: On-ice activities only run when the ice is thick enough. Andong said its Amsan Ice Festival needs at least 20–25 cm of ice; in 2026 some sections were under 3 cm and the festival was cancelled.
Last winter, mild weather pushed the Pyeongchang Trout Festival's opening from January 1 to January 9, and the Inje Smelt Festival was called off for a third straight year since 2024.
Delays, cancellations and early closings appear first on the organizer's website and social media. Check again on the morning you leave.
Never walk on river or reservoir ice outside the festival grounds. Safety checks only cover the designated areas inside the venue.

kids.title: With kids
items: Most ice and snow festivals, including Hwacheon, Pyeongchang, Hongcheon, Cheorwon, Pocheon and Taebaek, have sled slopes. Keep it short for young children and focus on sledding and snow play.
If the cold worries you, pick a venue with indoor areas (Hwacheon's indoor ice sculpture plaza, Hongcheon's indoor fishing) or a light festival for a short evening walk.
Strollers are hard to push on ice and snow, so a baby carrier is easier.

items.q: Are the 2026-27 winter festival dates out?
items.a: As of November 7, dates are out for the Haeundae Light Festival (Nov 29, 2026–Jan 18, 2027), the Garden of Morning Calm Lighting Festival (Dec 4, 2026–Mar 14, 2027), the Seoul Lantern Festival (Dec 11, 2026–Jan 31, 2027) and the Hwacheon Sancheoneo Ice Festival (Jan 9–31, 2027). The other eight haven't announced yet, so we show their usual timing from last season.

The organizer hasn't published this season's dates yet. We show the usual timing (early, mid or late month) based on when the festival actually ran last season and switch to real dates once they're announced. Even announced dates for ice festivals can change with the weather.

items.q: When is the 2027 Hwacheon Sancheoneo Ice Festival?
items.a: The official website lists January 9 (Sat) to January 31 (Sun), 2027, 23 days along Hwacheoncheon Stream. Last season it ran from January 10 to February 1, 2026.

items.q: Is the 2027 Pyeongchang Trout Festival January 9 to February 9?
items.a: As of November 7, those dates appear only as tentative dates on tour and listing sites; the organizer hasn't announced anything. Last season (Jan 9–Feb 9, 2026) was originally set to open on January 1 and was pushed back because of the weather.

items.q: How thick does the ice need to be for ice fishing?
items.a: It varies by festival. Andong said its Amsan Ice Festival needs at least 20–25 cm of ice. Some festivals, like Pyeongchang, measure the ice daily and stop ice fishing when it falls short. Never go onto ice outside the festival grounds.

items.q: Which winter festivals are good with kids?
items.a: Hwacheon and Hongcheon have sled slopes and indoor areas, and the Taebaeksan and Daegwallyeong snow festivals have snow sculptures and sledding. If the cold is a concern, a short evening walk at the Seoul Lantern Festival or Haeundae Light Festival works well.

The Seoul Lantern Festival, Haeundae Light Festival, Gwangbok-ro Winter Light Tree Festival and Hampyeong Winter Light Festival were free last season. The Garden of Morning Calm requires garden admission.
